A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DONUT research work. Their main text, equations, four tables, 23 figures, and supplementary sections A–F are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Argoverse 2 forecasting experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, difficult-turn evaluations, and failure analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original DONUT forecasting results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1–4 and qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The autoregressive decoder, proposer/refiner, overprediction objective, reference-point updates, losses, and appendix LineAttention component are retained. Added wording about mode attention and refinement clarifies the existing procedure rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Argoverse 2 single-agent forecasting, including the difficult-turn subset and the same failure and qualitative scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluated population is added or removed.

E2.justification: QCNet remains the encoder-decoder baseline, and Table 2 retains the same comparison methods and ensemble variants, including DeMo, SmartRefine, and SEPT. Comparator membership in the ablation and qualitative comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, 5-second history, 6-second prediction horizon, metrics, mode counts, and training settings remain unchanged. The new discussion of an effective 20-to-10-step overprediction horizon explains the existing refiner, rather than revising the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Table 1's component ablations, Figure 4's horizon analysis, and the supplementary LineAttention, efficiency, difficult-turn, failure-case, and qualitative analyses are retained. Removing the main-text mention of ablated-model visualizations does not remove those appendix panels.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 in v1 reports a minFDE standard error of 0.003 m across three training runs. v2 deletes both the uncertainty estimate and run count without replacement; this establishes reduced reporting, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: The limited numerical deletion is the 0.003 m standard-error result in Section 4.2. Tables 1–4 and the plotted predictions remain unchanged, including Table 2's DONUT b-minFDE6 of 1.79 and minFDE6 of 1.16.

T1.justification: The task definitions, mathematical formulation, distributional likelihoods, and Equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. The added explanation of refinement introduces no formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified decoder-only forecasting, auxiliary overprediction, and state-of-the-art non-ensemble Argoverse 2 performance. Wording edits do not alter these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a mechanism explanation for refinement–overprediction synergy: access to proposed trajectories and an updated reference point effectively reduces the overprediction horizon from 20 steps to 10. The existing efficiency limitations and failure-case discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 now explicitly states that mode attention connects modes of the same agent at the same time step, and that historical processing can run in parallel across agents and time steps. These clarify implementation details; hyperparameters, hardware, and tokenizer specifications are retained.

R1.justification: The same 56 referenced works and research positioning are retained. Changes to title capitalization, venue wording, and bibliographic metadata do not introduce or remove prior work.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract and several method and results paragraphs, standardizes 'time step', and regularizes bibliography wording. The section order, appendix structure, and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: There are small typography and text-flow changes, including Figure 6's 'time step' labels and project-link styling. All figures and tables retain their organization and displayed evidence; the appendix qualitative pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer technical wording and a useful explanation of refinement–overprediction synergy. However, it removes the only explicit three-run uncertainty result supporting training stability while retaining that argument and adding no validation. This modest loss of empirical transparency outweighs the limited explanatory gains.
